column7: Under the default security.require_mfa, a restricted account with no second factor (recover-admin's recovered admin, a one-time-password user, an admin-forced reset, pending first login) could never leave the restricted state: EnforceAccountRestriction refused /auth/mfa/enroll with PasswordChangeRequired and EnforceMFAEnrollment refused /auth/change-password with MFAEnrollmentRequired, so the documented lost-admin runbook ended in a permanent lockout whose only exits were insecure (require_mfa:false) or a backup restore. Replaced by one gate, server/middleware.EnforceAccountSetup, over core.PendingAccountSetupSteps: the union of the pending steps' routes (exact method + full path) plus GET profile, 403 with pending_steps on everything else. A login owing both steps gets a SetupOnly session capped at core.SetupSessionTTL (15 min, carried through refresh), revoked by core.EndSetupSessionIfComplete when the last step completes, so the next login is a normal two-step MFA login; an ordinary session owing both steps, or a SetupOnly session owing none, is refused 401. Found along the way and fixed in the same change: the ChangePassword handler tombstoned the caller's KEPT session in the auth cache (401 for invalidTokenTTL right after a password change, the #2978 bug class); now a delete-only clear. Proving tests: the route-registry guard (walks every /api/v1 route of the real router, red on main because the 403 carried no pending steps and mfa/enroll was refused) and TestAccountSetup_EitherOrder_EndsInMFALogin (every restricted population x both orders, red on main at the enrolment/password step); e2e scripts/e2e/journeys/journey20_recover_admin_mfa_test.go on the shipped config.
